question: How do I trace a custom multi-turn agent in Python?
answer:
To trace a custom multi-turn agent in Python, initialize Weave, then wrap the whole session in `weave.start_conversation()`. Wrap each user–agent exchange in `weave.start_turn()`, and wrap the model and tool calls inside each turn in `weave.start_llm()` and `weave.start_tool()`. Traces then appear in the **Agents** tab of your project [S1].

**Steps**
1. Run `pip install weave`, then call `weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")` before any `start_*` call. These tracing functions silently do nothing if init is missing or tracing is disabled [S3].
2. Use `start_conversation()` to group turns. A `conversation_id` you pass must stay stable for the life of the conversation. Reusing it adds turns to an existing conversation, and it's auto-generated if omitted. `agent_name` is optional, but without it the conversation isn't grouped under a named agent [S5].
3. Use `start_turn(user_message=..., model=...)` once per exchange. It creates an `invoke_agent` span that is the root of a new trace. It picks up the active conversation from context. If no conversation is active, the turn has no `conversation_id` and isn't grouped [S6].
4. Inside the turn, use `start_llm(...)` for each model call and `start_tool(...)` for each tool execution. The quickstart shows `llm.output(...)`, `llm.record(usage=weave.Usage(...))` and `tool.result = ...` [S7].
5. Each of these returns an object that works as a context manager (`with`) or can be closed manually with `.end()` [S4].

**Minimal sketch.** `call_model` and `run_tool` are placeholders for your own code, not Weave APIs. The quickstart's full OpenAI-based example includes token usage recording [S7].

```python
import weave

weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")

def run_turn(history, user_message):
    history.append({"role": "user", "content": user_message})   # you still keep the message history
    with weave.start_turn(user_message=user_message, model="my-model"):
        with weave.start_llm(model="my-model", provider_name="my-provider") as llm:
            reply = call_model(history)          # placeholder: returns text
            llm.output(reply)
        # if the model requested a tool:
        # with weave.start_tool(name="search", arguments="{...}", tool_call_id="1") as tool:
        #     tool.result = run_tool(...)        # placeholder
        history.append({"role": "assistant", "content": reply})
        return reply

with weave.start_conversation(agent_name="my-agent"):
    history = []
    for q in ["Hello", "And a follow-up?"]:
        run_turn(history, q)
```

The tracing context only groups the recorded spans. Your code still has to pass the accumulated `history` to the model each turn, as the quickstart does [S7].

If you use a supported agent SDK or harness, the docs point to autopatching integrations instead of manual instrumentation [S2].

# Trace your agents

> Use the Weave SDK to instrument multi-turn agentic applications and view them in the Agents tab.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tracing/instrument.md).

Learn how to instrument a multi-turn agentic application using the W\&B Weave SDK so that you can view, debug, and evaluate your agent's behavior. This guide is intended for developers who build or integrate agents and want structured visibility into conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool executions.

The Weave SDK for Agents models the full lifecycle of a multi-turn agent conversation: the agent that owns many conversations, the conversation that groups turns together, each user-agent exchange (turn), the LLM calls within a turn, and the tool executions that an LLM triggers. Traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project. Each conversation shows a multi-turn timeline with nested tool calls, token usage, and feedback.

Weave is built on [OpenTelemetry (OTel)](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/), the open standard for distributed tracing. Every turn, LLM call, and tool call emits an OTel *span* (a structured record of one operation). Each span is tagged with [GenAI semantic-convention](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) attributes like `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id`.

If you're tracing individual functions as Ops with the `@weave.op` decorator, see [Trace LLM applications](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md) instead.

Get the multi-turn chat view for a conversation.

Each turn corresponds to one trace.

**Args:**

```python theme={"system"}
client = weave.init("entity/project")
resp = client.get_agent_turns(conversation_id="...", limit=20)
for turn in resp.turns:

```

To trace a custom multi-turn agent in Python, initialize Weave, then wrap the whole session in `weave.start_conversation()`. Wrap each user–agent exchange in `weave.start_turn()`, and wrap the model and tool calls inside each turn in `weave.start_llm()` and `weave.start_tool()`. Traces then appear in the **Agents** tab of your project [S1].

**Steps**
1. Run `pip install weave`, then call `weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")` before any `start_*` call. These tracing functions silently do nothing if init is missing or tracing is disabled [S3].
2. Use `start_conversation()` to group turns. A `conversation_id` you pass must stay stable for the life of the conversation. Reusing it adds turns to an existing conversation, and it's auto-generated if omitted. `agent_name` is optional, but without it the conversation isn't grouped under a named agent [S5].
3. Use `start_turn(user_message=..., model=...)` once per exchange. It creates an `invoke_agent` span that is the root of a new trace. It picks up the active conversation from context. If no conversation is active, the turn has no `conversation_id` and isn't grouped [S6].
4. Inside the turn, use `start_llm(...)` for each model call and `start_tool(...)` for each tool execution. The quickstart shows `llm.output(...)`, `llm.record(usage=weave.Usage(...))` and `tool.result = ...` [S7].
5. Each of these returns an object that works as a context manager (`with`) or can be closed manually with `.end()` [S4].

**Minimal sketch.** `call_model` and `run_tool` are placeholders for your own code, not Weave APIs. The quickstart's full OpenAI-based example includes token usage recording [S7].

```python
import weave

weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")

def run_turn(history, user_message):
    history.append({"role": "user", "content": user_message})   # you still keep the message history
    with weave.start_turn(user_message=user_message, model="my-model"):
        with weave.start_llm(model="my-model", provider_name="my-provider") as llm:
            reply = call_model(history)          # placeholder: returns text
            llm.output(reply)
        # if the model requested a tool:
        # with weave.start_tool(name="search", arguments="{...}", tool_call_id="1") as tool:
        #     tool.result = run_tool(...)        # placeholder
        history.append({"role": "assistant", "content": reply})
        return reply

with weave.start_conversation(agent_name="my-agent"):
    history = []
    for q in ["Hello", "And a follow-up?"]:
        run_turn(history, q)
```

The tracing context only groups the recorded spans. Your code still has to pass the accumulated `history` to the model each turn, as the quickstart does [S7].

If you use a supported agent SDK or harness, the docs point to autopatching integrations instead of manual instrumentation [S2].
